descriptionByLocale.en:
Postdoctoral Researcher: Hydraulic stimulation and proppant behaviour in crystalline rock 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Chair of Engineering Geology and the BedrettoLab at ETH Zurich invites applications for a Postdoctoral Researcher position within the European research project UPLIFT, focusing on environmentally friendly hydraulic stimulation technologies in crystalline rock formations. The position is based at ETH Zurich and involves experimental research at the Bedretto Underground Laboratory. Hydraulic stimulation is a key technology for enhancing permeability in geothermal reservoirs. While multi-stage stimulation using proppants and chemical additives is widely applied in the oil and gas industry, its acceptance in Europe remains limited due to environmental concerns. Water-only stimulation approaches are more commonly accepted, yet their effectiveness compared to proppant-based methods particularly in crystalline rock remains insufficiently understood. The Bedretto Underground Laboratory provides a unique, highly instrumented environment to investigate coupled seismo-hydro-thermo-mechanical processes during hydraulic stimulation. Within the UPLIFT project, controlled laboratory and field-scale experiments will be conducted to evaluate water-only, proppant-based, and chemically assisted stimulation techniques. The goal is to develop safe, efficient, and environmentally acceptable stimulation strategies for geothermal applications across Europe. Job description
• Plan, conduct and analyse hydraulic stimulation experiments including proppant in vertical and horizontal boreholes (30–120 m scale) to investigate proppant transport, placement efficiency, and interaction with natural fracture networks
• Assess the effectiveness of different stimulation strategies and proppant placement approaches under varying geological conditions in terms of permeability enhancement and fracture geometry
• Collaborate with project partners performing small-scale laboratory experiments (GFZ) regarding joint interpretations and recommendations for the design full-scale hydraulic stimulation operations (e.g., Litoměřice site and other European contexts)
• Contribute to project deliverables and reporting, publish results in peer-reviewed journals and present findings at international conferences
• Collaborate closely with project UPLIFT partners (GFZ, various industry partners) and support coordination between experimental, modelling, and field activities Profile
• PhD in Engineeing Geology, Geophysics, Geomechanics, Earth Sciences, Physics, Engineering, or a related field
• Strong background in rock mechanics, hydrogeology, or reservoir engineering
• Experience with laboratory experiments and/or fieldwork in subsurface environments
• Willingness to participate in underground field campaigns
• Skills in numerical modelling (e.g., fracture mechanics, fluid flow)
• Strong programming skills (e.g., Python, MATLAB, or similar)
• Experience with seismic or fibre-optic sensing data is an asset
• Ability to work independently and lead research tasks within a collaborative environment
• Excellent communication skills in English Workplace Workplace We offer
• A fully funded postdoctoral position (initially 2 years, with possible extension)
• Employment according to ETH Zurich regulations
• Access to unique underground research infrastructure at BedrettoLab
• A dynamic, interdisciplinary and international research environment with strong links to academia and industry

Während die mehrstufige Stimulation mit Proppanten und chemischen Zusatzstoffen in der Öl- und Gasindustrie weit verbreitet ist, bleibt ihre Akzeptanz in Europa aufgrund von Umweltbelangen begrenzt. Wasser-only Stimulationsansätze werden häufiger akzeptiert, jedoch bleibt ihre Wirksamkeit gegenüber proppantbasierten Verfahren, insbesondere im kristallinen Gestein, unzureichend verstanden. Das Bedretto Underground Laboratory bietet eine einzigartige, hochinstrumentierte Umgebung, um gekoppelte seismo-hydro-thermo-mechanische Prozesse während der hydraulischen Stimulation zu untersuchen. Im Rahmen des UPLIFT-Projekts werden kontrollierte Labor- und Feldversuche durchgeführt, um Wasser-only, proppant-basierte und chemisch unterstützte Stimulationstechniken auszuwerten. Ziel ist es, sichere, effiziente und umweltverträgliche Stimulationsstrategien für geothermie Anwendungen in ganz Europa zu entwickeln. Jobbeschreibung

PhD Position: Optimization of shut-in strategies to reduce induced seismicity 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Chair of Engineering Geology and the BedrettoLab at ETH Zurich invite applications for a PhD position within a research project on poroelastic effects and induced seismicity in geothermal systems. The position focuses on post-shut-in seismicity and the design of safer operational protocols. Induced seismicity in geothermal systems often continues after injection or production is stopped, a phenomenon known as post-shut-in or trailing seismicity. In many cases, the largest seismic events occur after shut-in, posing challenges for hazard mitigation and operational safety. Despite extensive modelling efforts, the governing mechanisms are still not fully understood, and field observations of pressure and deformation during shut-in, that may improve our process understanding, are rare. This project exploits the unique monitoring capabilities of the Bedretto Underground Laboratory to investigate these processes and to develop experimentally validated guidelines for safer shut-in strategies. Job description
• Investigate pressure, deformation, and seismicity data from hydraulic stimulation experiments to derive conceptual models of post-shut-in processes
• Develop hydromechanical models to reproduce observed shut-in behaviour and test competing hypotheses (e.g., pressure diffusion vs. poroelastic effects)
• Develop/apply earthquake source physics models to understand induced seismicity processe
• Design and execute controlled hydraulic stimulation and production experiments with different shut-in protocols
• Quantify how different shut-in strategies influence seismicity rates and magnitudes
• Derive recommendations for optimized shut-in procedures to minimize induced seismic hazard
• Publish results, present at conferences, and contribute to project reporting Profile
• MSc degree in Engineering Geology, Geophysics, Seismology, Earth Sciences, Physics, Engineering, or a related field
• Interest in induced seismicity, geomechanics, and field experiments
• Strong quantitative and analytical skills
• Interest in learning complex numerical modelling tools

Postdoc position: Production-induced seismicity in fractured reservoirs 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Swiss Seismological Service (SED) and the BedrettoLab at ETH Zurich invite applications for a Postdoctoral Researcher position within a two-year research project on poroelastic effects and induced seismicity in geothermal systems. The position focuses on production-induced seismicity in fractured reservoirs and combines field experiments, data analysis, and numerical modelling. Project background Geothermal energy projects can induce seismicity during both fluid injection and fluid production through by complex hydromechanical processes in fractured rock. Development of simple and standardized modelling approaches to assess production-induced seismicity would benefit from insitu observations to identify relevant or missing hydromechanical processes and to calibrate models with. The project leverages the unique infrastructure of the Bedretto Underground Laboratory, where dense multiparametric monitoring networks provide unprecedented observations of pressure, deformation, and seismicity. The project aims at validating modelling approaches and practical workflows for assessing seismic hazard related to fluid production in Swiss geothermal projects (e.g. in Vaud and Geneva). Job description
• Analyse high-resolution pressure, deformation, and seismic datasets from past and new production experiments to identify governing hydromechanical processes
• Develop and apply coupled hydromechanical models (continuum and discontinuum) to reproduce observed behaviour and quantify poroelastic effects in fractured reservoirs

descriptionByLocale.en:
Machine Learning Scientist (AI-based Weather Forecasting) 100%, Locarno, fixed-term print Drucken Recent advances in AI-based weather prediction have demonstrated remarkable skill and computational efficiency. However, most current machine-learning weather prediction (MLWP) systems rely primarily on NWP analyses for initialization and only partially exploit the wealth of available satellite observations. With the advent of the Meteosat Third Generation (MTG), new high-frequency and high-resolution measurements of clouds, moisture, temperature, and lightning activity provide unprecedented opportunities for substantially improving regional forecasts. Project background Within the framework of a Research Fellowship supported by EUMETSAT, we are advancing the integration of geostationary satellite observations into a next-generation regional MLWP system. The project builds on an existing graph-based, stretched-grid regional forecasting model developed at MeteoSwiss and is embedded in the Anemoi framework initiated by ECMWF. The objective is to develop and evaluate novel multi-encoder-decoder architectures capable of ingesting various satellite data streams (e.g. radiances, cloud products, lightning observations, hyperspectral soundings) and integrating them into high-frequency forecasting cycles with lead times from short-range to up to 10 days ahead. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with national and international partners and contributes directly to the future operational exploitation of MTG data. Job description We are looking for a Scientific Programmer / Software Developer to join our motivated and interdisciplinary team. In this role, you will:
• Develop and implement machine-learning model architectures enabling the direct ingestion of next generation satellite data (e.g. MTG FCI, LI, IRS) into state-of-the-art regional forecasting models in Anemoi
• Contribute to the evolution of a multi-encoder-decoder MLWP framework within the Anemoi ecosystem
• Train, fine-tune, and evaluate models using large-scale meteorological and satellite datasets
• Quantify the impact of satellite data on forecast skill across variables and lead times
• Collaborate closely with scientists, ML researchers, and operational forecasting teams to ensure that forecast outputs meet the needs of diverse users
• Disseminate results through scientific publications, conference presentations, and exchanges with EUMETSAT and partner institutions We value people who enjoy solving complex problems, collaborating across disciplines, and contributing across different stages of the workflow as the system matures. This is a fixed-term contract of 1 year, with the possibility of extension for up to an additional 2 years. The main workplace is located at MeteoSwiss Locarno-Monti with regular visits to Zürich. The amount of remuneration will be in accordance with the salary system of ETH Zürich. Profile We welcome applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds who meet most (not necessarily all) of the following criteria:
• PhD in computer science, data science, natural sciences (e.g. physics, meteorology) or a related field. Candidates with an MSc and proven professional experience may also be considered
• Experience working with satellite data (e.g. geostationary observations, radiances, retrieval products)
• Strong programming skills in Python
• Experience in machine learning, ideally including deep learning architectures such as graph neural networks, transformers, or spatio-temporal models
• Experience with high-performance or distributed computing environments
• Good understanding of meteorological processes and numerical weather prediction
• Interest in DevOps practices and sustainable software engineering
• Ability to work independently on research questions while contributing to a collaborative team environment
• Motivation to work in a diverse, interdisciplinary, and international environment •

Il nostro gruppo di ricerca studia il ruolo cruciale delle nuvole e degli aerosol nel sistema climatico, mirando a comprendere meglio come i processi microfisici cloud spingano sia la formazione delle precipitazioni che l'impatto radiativo delle nuvole. Sfondo del progetto Questo ruolo supporta direttamente i nostri sforzi di ricerca costruendo gli strumenti che distribuiamo nel settore. Lo strumento primario è un imager olografico personalizzato sviluppato nel nostro gruppo. Utilizza olografia a percorso aperto in linea per catturare immagini 2D di particelle di nube in un volume ben definito. Con questo possiamo ricostruire la posizione, la forma e la dimensione delle gocce di nube come piccole come 5.5 µm e cristalli di ghiaccio fino a diversi millimetri. Il nostro ultimo sviluppo è una versione leggera di nome HOLIMOAir. Con due unità già completate, il piano è quello di costruire ulteriori 2–3 unità entro la fine dell'anno. Questo include fare adattamenti per garantire che siano adatti per le misurazioni del tunnel eolico e la distribuzione nell'Antartico.

Student Research Assistant – Development and assembly of instruments for atmospheric research 10%-30%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Atmospheric Physics group at ETH Zurich is looking for a Student Research Assistant to support the development and assembly of instruments used during field campaigns . Our research group studies the crucial role of clouds and aerosols in the climate system, aiming to better understand how cloud microphysical processes drive both precipitation formation and the radiative impact of clouds. Project background This role directly supports our research efforts by building the instruments we deploy in the field. The primary instrument is a custom holographic imager developed within our group. It uses in-line open-path holography to capture 2D images of cloud particles in a well-defined volume. With this we can reconstruct the position, shape, and size of cloud droplets as small as 5.5 µm and ice crystals up to several millimeters. Our latest development is a lightweight version named HOLIMOAir. With two units already completed, the plan is to build an additional 2–3 units by the end of the year. This includes making adaptations to ensure they are suitable for wind tunnel measurements and deployment in the Antarctic. Job description
• Building further HOLIMOAir units and develop upgrades for other instrumentation

Notre groupe de recherche étudie le rôle crucial des nuages et des aérosols dans le système climatique, en vue de mieux comprendre comment les processus microphysiques des nuages conduisent à la fois la formation de précipitations et l'impact radiatif des nuages. Contexte du projet Ce rôle appuie directement nos efforts de recherche en construisant les instruments que nous déployons sur le terrain. L'instrument principal est un imageur holographique personnalisé développé au sein de notre groupe. Il utilise l'holographie en ligne pour capturer des images 2D de particules de nuages dans un volume bien défini. Avec cela, nous pouvons reconstruire la position, la forme et la taille des gouttelettes de nuages aussi petites que 5.5 µm et des cristaux de glace jusqu'à plusieurs millimètres. Notre dernier développement est une version légère nommée HOLIMOAir. Avec deux unités déjà terminées, le plan est de construire 2 à 3 unités supplémentaires d'ici la fin de l'année. L'obiettivo primario è quello di favorire l'interazione tra circa 150 membri ZNZ, gruppi di ricerca basati su ETHZ, UZH e i quattro ospedali universitari, nella ricerca e nella formazione di neuroscienze. Ciò include lo sviluppo di infrastrutture innovative, il finanziamento per progetti collaborativi, la promozione della traduzione dei risultati della ricerca nella pratica clinica, la costruzione e il mantenimento dei rapporti con altri centri di ricerca in Svizzera e a livello internazionale, e la valorizzazione della consapevolezza pubblica dei risultati dei membri ZNZ. I ricercatori provenienti da sfondi tra cui biologia, medicina, psicologia, biochimica, fisica, ingegneria, informatica e economia indagano domande fondamentali su come il cervello funziona in salute e malattia. ZNZ Managing Director 80%-100%, Zurich, permanent print Drucken The Managing Director is responsible for implementing the objectives of the Neuroscience Center Zurich (ZNZ), a highly interdisciplinary research network jointly supported by ETH Zurich (ETHZ) and the University of Zurich (UZH). The primary goal is to foster interaction among approximately 150 ZNZ members—research groups based at ETHZ, UZH, and the four university hospitals—in neuroscience research and training. This includes developing innovative infrastructure, securing funding for collaborative projects, promoting the translation of research findings into clinical practice, building and maintaining relationships with other research centers in Switzerland and internationally, and enhancing public awareness of the achievements of ZNZ members. The Managing Director works closely with the ZNZ Steering Committee, which is responsible for the center’s overall strategy. Project background The landscape of neuroscience research within the ZNZ network is diverse. Researchers from backgrounds including biology, medicine, psychology, biochemistry, physics, engineering, computer science, and economics investigate fundamental questions about how the brain functions in health and disease. This drives the development of new diagnostics, therapies, and “intelligent” technologies. In recent years, ZNZ members have contributed significantly to advances in therapies for dementia, multiple sclerosis, and spinal cord injury, as well as to neurorehabilitation technologies, state-of-the-art brain imaging, focused ultrasound applications, sleep research, neuroeconomics, and artificial neural networks. Job description The Managing Director operates largely independently and bears significant responsibility for the overall success of the Center. As the role involves continuous interaction with a wide range of stakeholders it carries a high level of visibility. Problem-solving across multiple advisory boards can be complex and requires strong coordination and judgment. The Managing Director leads a small team and is responsible for:
• Promoting scientific collaboration among ZNZ research groups
• Providing organizational and financial support for selected ZNZ projects
• Maintaining and strengthening relationships with external research partners
• Managing ZNZ PhD grants and coordinating travel support for students
• Directing the International PhD Program in Neuroscience at UZH and ETH Zurich
• Overseeing the Specialized Master’s Program in Interdisciplinary Brain Sciences at UZH and ETH Zurich
• Leading communication with stakeholders, including newsletters, social media, and public events
• Participating in steering committees of related units at UZH
• Organizing regular events for ZNZ members, such as annual symposia and strategy meetings Profile

La posizione è ospitata dal gruppo Crop Science; un gruppo di lavoro vibrante e interdisciplinare nell'Istituto di Scienze Agrarie presso il Dipartimento di Scienze Ambientali dell'ETH di Zurigo. La ricerca fenotipante del nostro gruppo si concentra sullo sviluppo di metodi e modelli per determinare i tratti di rilevanza per l'allevamento di colture e test di varietà. Il gruppo di ricerca Agroscope Extension Arable Crops (Competence Division Plants and Plant Products) sviluppa soluzioni ecologiche per il controllo delle malattie, dei parassiti e delle infestanti e valuta le varietà vegetali per la loro idoneità in condizioni svizzere. Ci vuole un approccio olistico per creare sistemi agricoli sostenibili, convenienti e affidabili dal clima. Il progetto PhenoMix è un progetto congiunto di quattro gruppi di ricerca all'ETH di Zurigo, al Centro svizzero per la scienza dei dati e all'agroscopio. L'obiettivo generale di PhenoMix è quello di testare l'ipotesi che l'attuale tecnologia di fenotipazione del campo ad alto rendimento in combinazione con le valutazioni dei servizi fisiologici dell'impianto e dell'ecosistema può fornire una svolta per determinare genotipi che possono essere combinati con successo in miscele legume-cere agroecologicamente vantaggiose. Diverse varietà di legumi (peci, lenticchie) e cereali (wheat, avena, orzo) saranno coltivate in stand puri e in miscele sul campo fenotyping piattaforma FIP del gruppo Crop Science, in un campo sperimentale confinante e nei campi del contadino. I pacchetti di lavoro PhenoMix affrontano fenotyping, ecofisiologia vegetale, scienza dei dati e prestazioni agronomic-economiche con quattro studenti di dottorato, due postdoc e diversi tecnici assegnati a tali pacchetti di lavoro. Lo studente medico agro-economico istituirà e monitorerà esperimenti sul campo in loco e on-farm indagando su diverse miscele lentili-cereali valutando vari servizi ecosistemici. PhD Position: Agro-Economic Analysis of Legume-Cereal Mixtures (PhenoMix project) 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken This doctoral student position is part of the project “ PhenoMix: Multidimensional field phenotyping of crop mixtures ”, supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation. The position is hosted by the Crop Science group; a vibrant and interdisciplinary working group in the Institute of Agricultural Sciences at the Department of Environmental Systems Science at ETH Zurich. Our group’s phenotyping research focuses on the development of methods and models to determine traits of relevance for crop breeding and variety testing. The Agroscope research group Extension Arable Crops (Competence division Plants and Plant Products) develops ecological solutions for disease, pest and weed control and evaluates crop varieties for their suitability under Swiss conditions. It takes a holistic approach to create sustainable, cost-efficient, and climate-resilient arable farming systems. Project background PhenoMix is a joint project of four research groups at ETH Zurich, the Swiss Data Science Center and Agroscope. The overall objective of PhenoMix is to test the hypothesis that current high throughput field phenotyping technology in combination with plant physiological and ecosystem service assessments can provide a breakthrough to determine genotypes that can be successfully combined in agroecologically beneficial legume-cereal mixtures. Different varieties of legumes (peas, lentils) and cereals (wheat, oats, barley) will be grown in pure stands and in mixtures on the field phenotyping platform FIP of the Crop Science group, on a neighbouring experimental field and on farmer’s fields. The PhenoMix Work Packages address phenotyping, plant ecophysiology, data science, and agronomic-economic performance with four doctoral students, two postdocs and several technicians assigned to those work packages. The Agro-Economic doctoral student will establish and monitor on-site and on-farm field experiments investigating several lentil-cereal mixtures by assessing various ecosystem services. Job description This doctoral project will form an important cornerstone in the mosaic of the entire project with specific tasks and in alignment with the other PhenoMix doctoral students and postdocs for which recruiting is also going on currently. Overall tasks of the project include:
• Planning, conducting and evaluating field and post-harvest laboratory experiments
• Performing statistical analyses, including AI-based approaches
• Presentation of results at national and international events and publication in peer-reviewed and in practice-oriented journals
• Organisation of national workshops for growers, food industry and consumers
• Assistance in plot establishment, maintenance, monitoring, and harvest across all Work Packages of PhenoMi x. This full-time position is funded for four years. Salary and social benefits are provided according to ETH Zurich rules. The place of work will be at Agroscope in 8046 Zurich-Affoltern. Profile
• A MSc degree in agricultural sciences, biology, ecology or in a related field.
• Strong interest in applied interdisciplinary research and enjoyment of complex field experiments
• Experience in planning laboratory and field experiments as well as in statistical analyses (e.g. R)
• Performance-oriented, team player and open-minded personality
• Excellent standard of written and spoken English
• Good writing skills
• Driver’s license
• Experience in niche crops and good oral communication skills in German are beneficial Workplace Workplace We offer

Die phenotyping-Forschung unserer Gruppe konzentriert sich auf die Entwicklung von Methoden und Modellen, um die Relevanz für die Zucht- und Sortentests zu bestimmen. Die Agroscope-Forschungsgruppe Extension Arable Crops (Competence Division Plants and Plant Products) entwickelt ökologische Lösungen für Krankheit, Schädlingsbekämpfung und Unkrautbekämpfung und wertet Kultursorten für ihre Eignung unter Schweizer Bedingungen aus. Es geht um einen ganzheitlichen Ansatz, nachhaltige, kosteneffiziente und klimafreundliche landwirtschaftliche Systeme zu schaffen. Bitte geben Sie hier Text ein Projekt Hintergrund PhenoMix ist ein gemeinsames Projekt von vier Forschungsgruppen an der ETH Zürich, dem Swiss Data Science Center und Agroscope. Das Gesamtziel von PhenoMix ist es, die Hypothese zu testen, dass die aktuelle Hochdurchsatz-Feld-Phänotyping-Technologie in Kombination mit pflanzlichen physiologischen und Ökosystem-Service-Bewertungen einen Durchbruch bieten kann, um Genotypen zu bestimmen, die in agroökologisch nützlichen Legume-Cereal-Gemischen erfolgreich kombiniert werden können. Verschiedene Sorten von Hülsenfrüchten (Bäsen, Linsen) und Getreide (Weizen, Hafer, Gerste) werden in reinen Ständen und in Mischungen auf dem Feld Phänotyping Plattform FIP der Crop Science Gruppe, auf einem benachbarten Versuchsfeld und auf den Feldern des Landwirts angebaut. Ce poste est accueilli par le groupe Crop Science, un groupe de travail dynamique et interdisciplinaire de l'Institut des sciences agricoles du Département des sciences des systèmes environnementaux à l'ETH Zurich. Notre recherche de phénotypage de groupe se concentre sur l'élaboration de méthodes et de modèles pour déterminer les caractéristiques pertinentes pour la sélection des cultures et l'analyse des variétés. Le groupe de recherche Agroscope Extension Arable Crops (Division de la concurrence Plantes et produits végétaux) développe des solutions écologiques pour lutter contre les maladies, les ravageurs et les mauvaises herbes et évalue les variétés de cultures pour leur adéquation dans des conditions suisses. Il adopte une approche holistique pour créer des systèmes agricoles durables, rentables et résistants au climat. Veuillez saisir le texte ici Contexte du projet PhenoMix est un projet conjoint de quatre groupes de recherche à l'ETH Zurich, au Centre suisse des données scientifiques et à l'Agroscope. L'objectif global de PhenoMix est de tester l'hypothèse selon laquelle la technologie actuelle de phénotypage en champ à haut débit, combinée à des évaluations physiologiques des plantes et des services écosystémiques, peut fournir une percée pour déterminer les génotypes qui peuvent être combinés avec succès dans des mélanges de légumineuses-céréales bénéfiques sur le plan agroécologique. Différentes variétés de légumineuses (pois, lentilles) et de céréales (blé, avoine, orge) seront cultivées dans des peuplements purs et dans des mélanges sur la plateforme de phénotypage de champ FIP du groupe Crop Science, sur un champ expérimental voisin et sur les champs fermiers. Les packs de travail PhénoMix traitent du phénotypage, de l'écophysiologie végétale, de la science des données et de la performance agronomique et économique avec quatre doctorants, deux postdoctorants et plusieurs techniciens affectés à ces packs de travail. Le doctorant agro-économique établira et surveillera des expériences sur place et à la ferme portant sur plusieurs mélanges de lentilles-céréales en évaluant divers services écosystémiques. chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht Ricercatore Postdoctoral a Construction Heritage and Preservation 100%, Zurigo, stampa a tempo determinato Drucken La cattedra di Construction Heritage and Preservation è attualmente alla ricerca di un ricercatore post-dottorato a partire dal settembre 2026 o su accordo. La cattedra di patrimonio edilizio e conservazione si occupa di sfide teoriche e pratiche di raccolta, valutazione e conservazione dei monumenti. È affiliato all'Istituto per la conservazione e la storia delle costruzioni (IDB) e all'Istituto per la tecnologia in architettura (ITA) . La conoscenza dei metodi di costruzione tradizionali, dei materiali, dei principi di progettazione architettonica e dei processi di costruzione è essenziale per una gestione professionale e responsabile degli edifici storici. Per quanto riguarda il futuro sviluppo del patrimonio edilizio sembra altrettanto importante considerare i processi più giovani e anche attuali. Attualmente, vi è una mancanza di conoscenza circa l'invecchiamento e la riparabilità di tali nuove costruzioni e la ricerca sulle conseguenze a lungo termine per lo stock di edifici sembra insufficiente. La ricerca si concentra su diversi stock edilizi, sia più vecchi che più giovani (e anche molto giovani), domande del loro valore come monumenti e sfide relative alla loro conservazione. In questo contesto, i lavori di ingegneria strutturalmente eccezionali in Svizzera e gli esempi costruiti di processi e metodi di costruzione di nuova concezione sono di particolare interesse. Postdoctoral Researcher at Construction Heritage and Preservation 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Professorship of Construction Heritage and Preservation is currently searching for a postdoctoral researcher to start in September 2026 or upon agreement. Project background The Professorship of Construction Heritage and Preservation engages with theoretical and practical challenges of methodical collecting, assessing and preserving of monuments. It is affiliated with the Institute for Preservation and Construction History (IDB) as well as the Institute for Technology in Architecture (ITA) . Knowledge of traditional construction methods, materials, architectural design principles and building processes is essential for a professional and responsible handling of historic buildings. With regard to the future development of the building stock it seems equally important to consider younger and even current processes. New building materials, construction methods and “trends” are increasingly affecting architecture and an accelerated implementation of new ideas and technologies can be recognised in the building sector. Currently, there is a lack of knowledge about the aging and reparability of such new constructions and research on long-term consequences for the building stock seems inadequate. Research focusses on diverse building stocks, both older and younger (as well as very young), questions of their value as monuments and challenges concerning their conservation. Within this context, the structurally outstanding engineering works in Switzerland as well as the built examples of newly developed construction processes and methods are of special interest. Teaching activities include elective courses and core seminars which allow students to study and discuss current issues in-depth. The lecture concentrates on the theoretical and practical basics of preservation. Furthermore, the professorship offers the academic continuing education programs which comprehensively and methodologically combine high academic standards with practical relevance and impart specific professional skills. chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht PhD candidato per lo sviluppo di modelli multi-fisici di trasformatori a media frequenza ad alta potenza 100%, Zurigo, stampa a tempo fisso Drucken Il Laboratorio per sistemi elettronici ad alta potenza (HPE) presso il Dipartimento di tecnologia dell'informazione e ingegneria elettrica di ETH Zurigo conduce la ricerca internazionale leader sui sistemi di convertitori elettronici di potenza, che sono necessari, per esempio, nei futuri sistemi di distribuzione di energia elettrica per i Un'altra ricerca si concentra sui modulatori a impulsi a stato solido per applicazioni mediche (trattamento tomografia computer/cancro) e sugli acceleratori (CERN). Per la progettazione e l'ottimizzazione dei vari sistemi elettronici di potenza, sviluppiamo modelli multi-fisici avanzati / gemelli digitali / prototipi virtuali a livello di componenti e sistemi. Per un nuovo progetto di ricerca su Solid-State-Transformers per i futuri data center, stiamo cercando un: PhD candidate (100%) per lo sviluppo di modelli multi-fisici di trasformatori ad alta potenza a media frequenza Descrizione del lavoro Siamo alla ricerca di individui altamente motivati con un eccezionale background accademico che sono interessati a perseguire un dottorato nell'importante e multidisciplinare area di ricerca di modellazione e ottimizzazione di trasformatori ad alta potenza, a media frequenza (MFT). I trasformatori compatti e altamente efficienti che operano a frequenze kilohertz sono componenti chiave dei convertitori DC-DC ad alta potenza, che sono il componente principale dei trasformatori a stato solido (SST). Tali SST sono necessari, per esempio, in futuri data center AI, dove il consumo di energia per rack di computer aumenta a livelli di diverse centinaia di kilowatt o addirittura megawatt. Per trasferire l'energia in modo efficiente dalla rete a CPU/GPU, sono necessarie tensioni di sistema più elevate nei centri di dati / rack per computer, e sistemi di convertitori elettronici di potenza efficienti basati su SST sono essenziali per il controllo del flusso di potenza altamente dinamico. Per spingere i limiti di efficienza e densità di potenza di questi SST si svilupperà modelli multi-fisici di trasformatori, che descrivono non solo le perdite (HF) nell'avvolgimento e nel nucleo, ma anche la distribuzione di raffreddamento / temperatura nel trasformatore, risonanze nell'avvolgimento a causa di capacità parassitarie, e isolamento elettrico. Si lavorerà anche sull'ottimizzazione della geometria del nucleo e dell'avvolgimento, lo sviluppo di concetti di raffreddamento avanzati per gli avvolgimento e il core, e la progettazione di soluzioni per collegare efficacemente gli avvolgimento ad alta corrente. Utilizzando i modelli e i concetti sviluppati, si identificherà le barriere tecnologiche per la potenza trasferibile e l'efficienza dei MFT. I modelli sviluppati dovrebbero essere integrati in procedure di ottimizzazione per sistemi di convertitori elettronici di potenza in modo computazionalmente efficiente. Ciò è essenziale per ottenere efficienze di sistema eccezionali e densità di potenza, così come ottenere un vantaggio competitivo. I modelli fanno parte anche di un continuo e più ampio progetto di sviluppo del framework di modellazione presso HPE, offrendo l'opportunità di collaborare con altri candidati PhD su diversi aspetti di modellazione. Per verificare i nuovi concetti e modelli sviluppati, si progetta e costruisce prototipi MFT, compresi i sistemi di conversione, per operare i MFT in condizioni realistiche. Profilo

PhD candidate for developing multi-physics models of high-power medium frequency transformers 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Laboratory for High Power Electronic Systems (HPE) at the Department of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering of ETH Zurich conducts internationally leading research on power electronic converter systems, which are required, for example, in future energy distribution systems for the integration of renewable energy sources or in traction applications/electric vehicles. Another research focus is on solid-state pulse modulators for medical applications (computer tomography/cancer treatment) and accelerators (CERN). For the design and optimisation of the various power electronic systems, we develop advanced multi-physics models/digital twins/virtual prototypes at the component and system level. For a new research project on Solid-State-Transformers for future data centres, we are looking for a: PhD candidate (100%) for developing multi-physics models of high-power medium frequency transformers Job description We are looking for highly motivated individuals with an outstanding academic background who are interested in pursuing a PhD in the important and multidisciplinary research area of modelling and optimising high-power, medium-frequency transformers (MFTs). Compact, highly efficient transformers that operate at kilohertz frequencies are key components of high-power DC-DC converters, which are the core component of solid-state transformers (SSTs). Such SSTs are required, for example, in future AI data centres, where power consumption per computer rack increases to levels of several hundred kilowatts or even megawatts. To transfer energy efficiently from the grid to CPUs/GPUs, higher system voltages are required in data centres/computer racks, and efficient power electronics converter systems based on SSTs are essential for controlling the highly dynamic power flow. For pushing the efficiency and power density limits of these SSTs you will develop multi-physics models of transformers, which describe not only the (HF) losses in the winding and the core, but also the cooling/temperature distribution in the transformer, resonances in the winding due to parasitic capacitances, and electrical insulation. You will also work on optimising the core and winding geometry, developing advanced cooling concepts for the windings and core, and designing solutions for efficiently connecting the high-current windings. Using the models and concepts developed, you will then identify technological barriers to the transferable power and efficiency of MFTs. The developed models should be integrated into optimisation procedures for power electronic converter systems in a computationally efficient way. This is essential for achieving outstanding system efficiencies and power densities, as well as gaining a competitive edge. The models are also part of an ongoing, wider modelling framework development project at HPE, offering the opportunity to collaborate with other PhD candidates on different modelling aspects. For verifying the new concepts and developed models, you will design and build MFT prototypes, including converter systems, to operate the MFTs under realistic conditions. Profile

• Fundamental knowledge of power electronic converter systems
• Good communication skills
• Fluency in English
• The willingness to fully commit yourself as part of an international team.
• In addition, you should be interested in the detailed modelling and design of magnetic components and the optimisation of power electronic systems. Workplace Workplace We offer

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht PhD-Kandidat für die Entwicklung von Multi-Physik-Modellen von Hochleistungs-Mittelfrequenztransformatoren 100%, Zürich, Festdruck Drucken Das Labor für High Power Electronic Systems (HPE) am Department of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering der ETH Zürich führt international führende Forschungen zu Stromelektronik-Konvertersystemen durch, die beispielsweise in zukünftigen Energieverteilungssystemen für die Integration erneuerbarer Energieträger oder Zugfahrzeuge benötigt werden. Ein weiterer Forschungsschwerpunkt sind Festkörper-Impulsmodulatoren für medizinische Anwendungen (Computertomographie/Krebsbehandlung) und Beschleuniger (CERN). Für die Gestaltung und Optimierung der verschiedenen leistungselektronischen Systeme entwickeln wir fortschrittliche multiphysikalische Modelle/digitale Zwillinge/virtueller Prototypen auf Bauteil- und Systemebene. Für ein neues Forschungsprojekt zu Solid-State-Transformern für zukünftige Rechenzentren suchen wir einen: PhD-Kandidat (100%) für die Entwicklung von Multi-Physik-Modellen von Hochleistungs-Mittelfrequenztransformatoren Jobbeschreibung Wir suchen hoch motivierte Personen mit einem hervorragenden akademischen Hintergrund, die daran interessiert sind, einen Doktortitel im wichtigen und multidisziplinären Forschungsbereich der Modellierung und Optimierung von hochleistungsfähigen, mittelfrequenten Transformatoren (MFTs) zu verfolgen. Kompakte, hocheffiziente Transformatoren, die bei Kilohertz-Frequenzen arbeiten, sind Schlüsselkomponenten von Hochleistungs-DC-Wandlern, die Kernkomponente von Festkörpertransformatoren (SSTs). Solche SSTs sind beispielsweise in zukünftigen KI-Datenzentren erforderlich, wo der Stromverbrauch pro Computer-Rack auf mehrere hundert Kilowatt oder sogar Megawatt ansteigt. Um Energie effizient vom Netz auf CPUs/GPUs zu übertragen, sind höhere Systemspannungen in Rechenzentren/Computer-Racks erforderlich und effiziente Stromelektronik-Wandlersysteme auf Basis von SSTs sind für die Steuerung des hochdynamischen Leistungsflusses unerlässlich. Um die Effizienz- und Leistungsdichtegrenzen dieser SSTs zu schieben, entwickeln Sie mehrphysikalische Modelle von Transformatoren, die nicht nur die (HF) Verluste in der Wicklung und dem Kern beschreiben, sondern auch die Kühl-/Temperaturverteilung im Transformator, Resonanzen in der Wicklung durch parasitäre Kapazitäten und elektrische Isolation. Sie arbeiten auch daran, die Kern- und Wickelgeometrie zu optimieren, fortschrittliche Kühlkonzepte für Wicklungen und Kern zu entwickeln und Lösungen für eine effiziente Verbindung der Hochstromwicklungen zu entwickeln. Mit den entwickelten Modellen und Konzepten werden Sie dann technologische Barrieren für die übertragbare Leistung und Effizienz von MFTs identifizieren. Die entwickelten Modelle sollten rechnerisch effizient in Optimierungsverfahren für stromelektronische Wandlersysteme integriert werden. Dies ist wichtig, um hervorragende Systemeffizienzen und Leistungsdichten zu erzielen und einen Wettbewerbsvorteil zu gewinnen. Die Modelle sind auch Teil eines laufenden, breiteren Modellierungs-Rahmenentwicklungsprojekts bei HPE und bieten die Möglichkeit, mit anderen PhD-Kandidaten zu verschiedenen Modellierungsaspekten zusammenzuarbeiten. Um die neuen Konzepte und entwickelten Modelle zu überprüfen, entwerfen und bauen Sie MFT-Prototypen, einschließlich Konvertersysteme, um die MFTs unter realistischen Bedingungen zu betreiben. Profil

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht Candidat au doctorat pour le développement de modèles multiphysiques de transformateurs haute puissance à moyenne fréquence 100%, Zurich, tirage à terme fixe Drucken Le Laboratoire de systèmes électroniques haute puissance (HPE) du Département de technologie de l'information et de génie électrique de l'ETH Zurich mène des recherches de pointe sur les systèmes de convertisseurs électroniques de puissance, qui sont nécessaires, par exemple, dans les futurs systèmes de distribution d'énergie pour l'intégration de sources d'énergie renouvelables ou dans les applications de traction/véhicules électriques. Un autre axe de recherche porte sur les modulateurs d'impulsions à l'état solide pour les applications médicales (tomographie par ordinateur/traitement du cancer) et les accélérateurs (CERN). Pour la conception et l'optimisation des différents systèmes électroniques de puissance, nous développons des modèles multi-physiques avancés, des jumeaux numériques et des prototypes virtuels au niveau des composants et du système. Pour un nouveau projet de recherche sur Solid-State-Transformers pour les futurs centres de données, nous sommes à la recherche d'un candidat au doctorat (100 %) pour développer des modèles multiphysiques de transformateurs à moyenne fréquence haute puissance. Nous recherchons des personnes hautement motivées ayant une formation universitaire exceptionnelle qui sont intéressées à poursuivre un doctorat dans le domaine important et multidisciplinaire de la recherche de modélisation et d'optimisation des transformateurs haute puissance et moyenne fréquence (MFT). Les transformateurs compacts et hautement efficaces qui fonctionnent à des fréquences kilohertz sont des composants clés des convertisseurs DC-DC de haute puissance, qui sont la composante centrale des transformateurs à l'état solide (SST). Ces SST sont nécessaires, par exemple, dans les futurs centres de données AI, où la consommation d'énergie par rack d'ordinateur augmente à des niveaux de plusieurs centaines de kilowatts, voire mégawatts. Pour transférer efficacement l'énergie du réseau vers les CPU/GPU, des tensions plus élevées sont nécessaires dans les centres de données/racks d'ordinateur, et des systèmes de convertisseur électronique de puissance efficaces basés sur les SST sont essentiels pour contrôler le flux de puissance très dynamique. Pour repousser les limites d'efficacité et de densité de puissance de ces SST, vous développerez des modèles multiphysiques de transformateurs, qui décrivent non seulement les pertes (HF) dans l'enroulement et le noyau, mais aussi la distribution de refroidissement/température dans le transformateur, les résonances dans l'enroulement dues aux capacités parasitaires, et l'isolation électrique. Vous travaillerez également sur l'optimisation de la géométrie du noyau et de l'enroulement, le développement de concepts de refroidissement avancés pour les enroulements et le noyau, et la conception de solutions pour raccorder efficacement les enroulements à haut courant. En utilisant les modèles et les concepts développés, vous identifierez ensuite les obstacles technologiques à la puissance transférable et à l'efficacité des MFT. Les modèles développés devraient être intégrés dans les procédures d'optimisation des systèmes de convertisseur électronique de puissance d'une manière efficace par calcul. C'est essentiel pour atteindre des gains d'efficacité et des densités de puissance remarquables et pour obtenir un avantage concurrentiel. Les modèles s'inscrivent également dans le cadre d'un projet d'élaboration d'un cadre de modélisation plus large et en cours à HPE, offrant la possibilité de collaborer avec d'autres candidats au doctorat sur différents aspects de la modélisation. Pour vérifier les nouveaux concepts et modèles développés, vous concevez et construisez des prototypes MFT, y compris des systèmes de conversion, pour utiliser les MFT dans des conditions réalistes. Profil

L'Innosuisse-Flagship SWIRCULAR è gestito da un consorzio di istituti di ricerca svizzeri e partner industriali che perseguono un obiettivo comune: la trasformazione dell'industria edile svizzera mediante procedure circolari. Il consorzio offre una vasta gamma di know-how e si estende su tutte le fasi del ciclo di vita. Ciò garantisce che le innovazioni nel campo della costruzione circolare siano efficacemente sviluppate e realizzate con successo. Il progetto 5 "Value Preservation for Circular Practice", guidato dalla Cattedra del Patrimonio delle costruzioni e della cura dei monumenti, mira a scoprire e promuovere le qualità intrinseche e il potenziale del patrimonio edilizio esistente. Nell'ambito del progetto, i componenti vengono sistematicamente raccolti (ricerca e inventario di costruzione), che identificano i valori incorporati e sviluppano misure di riabilitazione e riparazione innovative e scalabili. I risultati vengono poi trasmessi all'intero Öcosistema dell'economia circolare.

chevron left Overview chevron left Overview Scientific:r Staff:in, Chair of Construction and Heritage (m/w/d) 80%-100%, Zurich, limited print Print As part of the Innosuisse flagship project SWIRCULAR, the professorship for construction heritage and preservation is looking for a:n scientific:n staff:in early summer 2026 or by agreement. The Innosuisse-Flagship SWIRCULAR is run by a consortium of Swiss research institutions and industrial partners who pursue a common goal: the transformation of the Swiss construction industry by using circular procedures. The consortium offers a wide range of know-how and extends over all phases of the life cycle. This ensures that innovations in the field of circular construction are effectively developed and successfully implemented. The 5 "Value Preservation for Circular Practice" project, led by the Chair of Construction Heritage and Monument Care, aims to discover and promote the inherent qualities and potential of the existing building stock. As part of the project, components are systematically collected (construction research and inventory), which identify values embedded therein and develop innovative and scalable rehabilitation and repair measures. The results are then passed on to the entire Öcosystem of the circular economy.

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht Postdoctoral Position in Climate Science 100%, Zurigo, stampa a tempo fisso Drucken Invitiamo applicazioni per una posizione Postdoc a tempo pieno nel gruppo di Fisica Climatica del Prof. Reto Knutti e Prof. Erich Fischer presso l'Istituto per la scienza dell'atmosfera e del clima dell'ETH di Zurigo con l'obiettivo di comprendere e quantificare gli estremi climatici e climatici in un clima caldo. Sfondo del progetto La posizione Postdoc sarà parte integrante del nuovo centro nazionale di competenza nella ricerca NCCR CLIM+. NCCR CLIM+ supporta la trasformazione della Svizzera verso una società responsabile del clima e forma una nuova generazione di esperti con una forte competenza disciplinare e transdisciplinare. Questo progetto offre l'opportunità di collaborare con esperti leader nella scienza dell'atmosfera e del clima all'interno del NCCR CLIM+ e dell'ETH Zurigo. Descrizione del lavoro
• Stiamo cercando scienziati del clima fisico con esperienza di ricerca nello studio degli estremi climatici e climatici utilizzando modelli di sistemi globali e terrestri accoppiati, modelli di clima e convezione regionali, modelli meteorologici AI o nell'utilizzo di analisi di processo o statistica dei risultati e rianalisi dei modelli
• Il richiedente dovrebbe contribuire al NCCR CLIM+ e prendere la leadership nel campo della ricerca, compresa la supervisione degli studenti
• La posizione è inizialmente di due anni e può essere estesa in base alle prestazioni e alla disponibilità di finanziamenti
• • I candidati devono avere un PhD in fisica, scienze atmosferiche e climatiche, statistiche o materie correlate, la conoscenza idealmente di lavoro dei modelli climatici, e l'esperienza con lo scripting delle conchiglie, l'informatica ad alte prestazioni, o le statistiche avanzate e i quadri di analisi dei dati (python, R)
• Indipendentemente dal background, i candidati di successo avranno una personalità interattiva, la motivazione per lavorare con i modelli climatici numerici all'avanguardia Offriamo un ambiente di ricerca dinamico e stimolante, eccellenti condizioni di lavoro, infrastrutture di supercomputing, e un grande grado di libertà per i candidati di successo di portare nelle proprie idee e esperienze di ricerca
• L'Istituto per la scienza dell'atmosfera e del clima a ETH Zurigo è un istituto leader mondiale nel campo della ricerca sul cambiamento climatico globale e regionale in una delle principali università internazionali per le scienze naturali e la tecnologia chevron right Lavoro, insegnamento e ricerca a ETH Zurigo In linea con i nostri valori, ETH Zurich incoraggia una cultura inclusiva. Promuoviamo l'uguaglianza di opportunità, la diversità di valore e nutrire un ambiente di lavoro e di apprendimento in cui i diritti e la dignità di tutto il nostro staff e gli studenti sono rispettati. Visita il nostro sito Equal Opportunities and Diversity per scoprire come garantiamo un ambiente equo e aperto che permetta a tutti di crescere e fiorire. La sostenibilità è un valore fondamentale per noi – stiamo costantemente lavorando verso un futuro neutro dal clima. Curioso? Anche noi. Postdoctoral Position in Climate Science 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken We invite applications for a full-time Postdoc position in the Climate Physics group of Prof. Reto Knutti and Prof. Erich Fischer at the Institute for Atmospheric and Climate Science at ETH Zurich with a focus on understanding and quantifying weather and climate extremes in a warming climate. Project background The Postdoc position will be an integral part of the newly established National Competence Centre in Research NCCR CLIM+ . NCCR CLIM+ supports Switzerland’s transformation towards a climate-resilient society and trains a new generation of experts with strong disciplinary and transdisciplinary expertise. This project offers the opportunity to collaborate with leading experts in atmospheric and climate science within the NCCR CLIM+ as well as ETH Zurich. Job description
• We are seeking physical climate scientists with research experience in studying weather and climate extremes using coupled global and Earth System Models, regional climate and convection-permitting models, or AI weather models or in using process-based or statistical analysis of model results and reanalyses
• The applicant is expected to contribute to NCCR CLIM+ and to take leadership in the research field, including the supervision of students
• The position is for two years initially and can be extended subject to performance and availability of funding
• The starting date is as soon as possible but can be negotiated Profile
• Applicants must have a PhD in physics, atmospheric and climate sciences, statistics or related subjects, ideally working knowledge of climate models, and experience with shell scripting, high performance computing, or advanced statistics and data analysis frameworks (python, R)
• Regardless of background, the successful applicants will have an interactive personality, motivation to work with cutting-edge numerical climate models and their output, the ability to carry out research in an interdisciplinary and international environment, and a strong desire to disseminate results in conference talks and journal articles
• Fluency in English (written and spoken) and strong communication skills, in particular experience in the publication of research results in peer-reviewed journals, is required Workplace Workplace We offer
• We offer a dynamic and inspiring research environment, excellent work conditions, supercomputing infrastructure, and a large degree of freedom for the successful candidates to bring in their own research ideas and experience
• The Institute for Atmospheric and Climate Science at ETH Zurich is a world-leading institute in the field of research on global and regional climate change at one of the leading international universities for natural sciences and technology chevron_right Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future . Curious? So are we. We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:
• CV
• Publication list and brief paragraphs highlighting three scientific achievements
• Motivation statement and research ideas
• Names and contact details of three professional references Please include a detailed statement of motivation, scientific achievements and research ideas that you would be keen to work on in the context of this position. Application deadline is 30 May 2026 , but review of applications will continue until the positions are filled

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht Position postdoctorale en sciences du climat 100%, Zurich, tirage à terme fixe Drucken Nous invitons les candidatures pour un poste postdoc à temps plein dans le groupe de physique du climat du Prof. Reto Knutti et Prof. Erich Fischer à l'Institut des sciences de l'atmosphère et du climat à l'ETH Zurich, en mettant l'accent sur la compréhension et la quantification des phénomènes météorologiques et climatiques extrêmes dans un climat de réchauffement. Contexte du projet Le poste Postdoc fera partie intégrante du nouveau Centre national de compétence en recherche NCCR CLIM+ . NCCR CLIM+ soutient la Suisse dans sa transformation vers une société résiliente au climat et forme une nouvelle génération d'experts possédant une solide expertise disciplinaire et transdisciplinaire. Ce projet offre l'occasion de collaborer avec des experts de premier plan en sciences atmosphériques et climatiques au sein du NCCR CLIM+ ainsi qu'à l'ETH Zurich. Description du poste
• Nous recherchons des scientifiques du climat physique ayant une expérience de recherche dans l'étude des phénomènes météorologiques et climatiques extrêmes à l'aide de modèles couplés de systèmes planétaires et terrestres, de modèles régionaux de climat et de convection, ou de modèles météorologiques d'IA ou dans l'analyse statistique des résultats et des réanalyses des modèles par processus
• Le candidat devrait contribuer au NCCR CLIM+ et prendre le leadership dans le domaine de la recherche, y compris la supervision des étudiants
• Le poste est initialement de deux ans et peut être prolongé sous réserve de la performance et de la disponibilité du financement
• La date de début est le plus tôt possible, mais peut être négociée Profil
• Les candidats doivent avoir un doctorat en physique, sciences atmosphériques et climatiques, statistiques ou sujets connexes, idéalement des connaissances de travail des modèles climatiques, et l'expérience avec le script shell, l'informatique à haute performance, ou des statistiques avancées et des cadres d'analyse de données (python, R)
• Quel que soit le contexte, les candidats retenus auront une personnalité interactive, la motivation de travailler avec des modèles numériques de pointe et leur production, la capacité de mener des recherches dans un environnement interdisciplinaire et international, et une forte volonté de diffuser les résultats dans des conférences et des articles de revues

Scientific Collaborator / Teaching Assistant 50%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken We are looking for a Scientific Collaborator / Teaching Assistant to join our team at ETH Zürich from July 2026 or by agreement. As part of the team, you will contribute to teaching and course preparation, including giving inputs and tutorials, organizing lectures, facilitating discussions, and supporting the writing and editing of academic and teaching-related texts. Project background Studio Maria Conen The Chair of Architecture and Housing approaches architecture as an ecological, social, and material practice shaping forms of living together. It addresses climate adaptation, resource cycles, and housing as a relational system embedded within landscape, water, and infrastructure. The Chair develops architecture as a mediating discipline, where spatial, material, and environmental logics converge. Through design and research, housing is understood as an interconnected, multi-scalar construct that integrates regenerative design, circular processes, and the interplay between natural and built systems. A particular focus lies on water as a spatial and formative driver, alongside a continuous exploration of form as a means to address these questions. Through teaching, research, and collaboration, the Chair fosters experimental design practices grounded in observation, making, and critical reflection, aiming to produce a precise and strong design for contemporary habitation. Job description For our Bachelor’s and Master’s design studio, we are looking for a part-time Teaching Assistant (50%).
• Teaching days: Tuesday and Wednesday
• Additional 10% workload distributed throughout the week The role includes:
• Contributing to teaching and course preparation, including inputs, tutorials, lectures, and discussions
• Preparing and supporting seminar weeks and study trips, including organizational and content-related tasks
• Supporting the writing and editing of academic and teaching-related texts We are looking for candidates with a strong interest in:
• Reuse and circular thinking
• Biodiversity and ecology
• Landscape
• Architectural representation (drawings, photography, models)
• Housing Responsibilities
• Prepare and organise teaching materials for the design studio
• Support and guide students in developing their projects (concept, structure, detailing)
• Provide technical and architectural expertise
• Contribute to the writing, editing, and proofreading of academic, research, and teaching-related texts Profile
• Degree in Architecture with 2–3 years of professional experience
• Strong design and technical skills
• Interest in academic teaching and research
• High level of initiative, strong communication skills, and a collaborative yet independent working style
• Fluency in English and German
• Preferably pursuing or planning to establish an independent practice Workplace Workplace We offer
• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

descriptionByLocale.it:
Descrizione Ricerca post-dottorale in termini di genomica e diversità transposonale comparata 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il nuovo gruppo Plant Disease Dynamics dell'ETH di Zurigo sta cercando di reclutare un biologo fungo del genoma interessato ai modi in cui i transposoni modellano la struttura e la funzione dei genoma patogeni vegetali. Stiamo cercando qualcuno con esperienza precedente sia in genomica comparativa fungina o transposon, che può esplorare la diversità e l'evoluzione dei transposons di Starship e dei geni e transposizioni che portano all'interno di specie fungine infettanti vegetali. Questa posizione costituisce un pilastro di un progetto di ricerca a tre pilastri, dove sarete associati con altri esperti in biochimica e biologia cellulare. L'obiettivo è quello di costruire un team interdisciplinare collaborativo che utilizza la genomica della popolazione per sostenere lo sviluppo di un'implementazione di modelli di transposon sperimentali di lavoro in laboratorio. Sfondo del progetto Il trasferimento genico orizzontale (HGT) consente la diffusione di geni patogeni tra i microbi e può quindi guidare l'emergenza di nuove malattie. Nei funghi patogeni, una minaccia globale emergente sia per gli esseri umani che per i nostri raccolti, i meccanismi che facilitano la HGT rimangono sconosciuti. Recenti lavori hanno scoperto un nuovo gruppo di transponti giganti chiamati Starships, che hanno mosso virulence, la tolleranza dei metalli e altri geni associati al fitness orizzontalmente tra le specie fungine. Questa posizione post-doctoral è focalizzata sui funghi patogeni vegetali, Bipolaris sorokiniana, Parastagonospora nodorum e Pyrenophora tritici-repentis che portano tutti il gene fungine di virulenza ToxA , che è annidato all'interno di un transposon passeggeri più piccolo chiamato ToxTA. Questo transposon è stato catturato indipendentemente da due diversi trasposizioni di Starship, Sanctuary e Horizon con la prova di altre catture in altre specie fungine. Cerchiamo di comprendere la storia evolutiva e il trasferimento orizzontale del transposon ToxTA nelle popolazioni naturali di tutte le specie fungine in cui si trova. Questo include oltre 300 genoma pubblicamente accessibili, così come diverse dozzine di assemblee di lunga data della collezione interna del laboratorio. Questa posizione mira a sintetizzare tutte le informazioni disponibili da questi isolati fungini naturali per costruire ipotesi per le quali le caratteristiche genetiche sono essenziali per il trasferimento orizzontale. Post-Doctoral Research in Comparative Fungal Genomics and Transposon Diversity 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The newly established Plant Disease Dynamics group at the ETH Zurich is looking to recruit a fungal genome biologist interested in the ways in which transposons shape the structure and function of plant pathogen genomes. We are looking for someone with prior experience in either fungal or transposon comparative genomics, who can explore the diversity and evolution of Starship transposons and the genes and transposons they carry within plant infecting fungal species. This position forms one pillar of a three-pillared research project, where you will be partnered with other experts in biochemistry and cell biology. The goal is to build a collaborative interdisciplinary team that uses population genomics to support the development an implementation of working experimental transposon models in the lab. Project background Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) enables the spread of pathogenicity genes between microbes and can therefore drive the emergence of novel diseases . In pathogenic fungi, an emerging global threat to both humans and our crops, the mechanisms that facilitate HGT remain unknown. Recent work has uncovered a novel group of giant transposons called Starships, which have moved virulence, metal tolerance and other fitness associated genes horizontally between fungal species. This post-doctoral positions is focused on the plant pathogenic fungi, Bipolaris sorokiniana, Parastagonospora nodorum and Pyrenophora tritici-repentis that all carry the fungal virulence gene ToxA , which is nested inside a smaller passenger transposon called ToxTA. This transposon has been captured independently by two different Starship transposons, Sanctuary and Horizon with evidence of other captures in other fungal species. We seek to understand the evolutionary history and horizontal transfer of the ToxTA transposon in natural populations of all fungal species in which it is found. This includes over 300 publicly accessible genomes as well as several dozen long-read assemblies from the lab's internal collection. This position aims to synthesise all available information from these natural fungal isolates to build hypotheses for which genetic features are essential for horizontal transfer. Job description
• Generate new long-read Nanopore assemblies from the labs long-term culture collection
• Assemble, annotate and quality assess all existing 30+ long-read genome assemblies
• Mine availalbe public genomes for TEs of interest
• Establish reproducible Snakemake/Nextflow pipelines to support the labs long-term research interests
• Proactively manage the labs genomic data resources
• Supervise and mentor PhD and Masters students in comparative fungal genomics
• Assist in the delivery of lectures or seminars for the Plant Disease Dynamics group
• Write and publish peer-reviewed manuscripts
• Apply for funding to develop research independence The initial contract duration is two years, with the possibility of extension. Profile

Beschreibung Post-Doctoral Research in Comparative Fungal Genomics and Transposon Diversity 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Die neu gegründete Plant Disease Dynamics-Gruppe an der ETH Zürich sucht einen Pilz-Genom-Biologe zu rekrutieren, der an der Art interessiert ist, wie Transposons die Struktur und Funktion von Pflanzenpathogen-Genomen prägen. Wir suchen jemanden mit vorheriger Erfahrung in entweder Pilz- oder Transposon vergleichende Genomik, die die Vielfalt und Evolution von Sternenschiff-Transposons und die Gene und Transposons, die sie in Pflanzen infizieren Pilzarten zu erforschen. Diese Position bildet eine Säule eines dreifachen Forschungsprojekts, in dem Sie mit anderen Experten in der Biochemie und Zellbiologie zusammenarbeiten werden. Ziel ist es, ein kollaboratives interdisziplinäres Team aufzubauen, das die Bevölkerungsgenomik nutzt, um die Entwicklung einer Implementierung von funktionierenden experimentellen Transposonmodellen im Labor zu unterstützen. Projekt Hintergrund Der horizontale Gentransfer (HGT) ermöglicht die Ausbreitung von Pathogenitätsgenen zwischen Mikroben und kann daher das Auftreten neuer Krankheiten antreiben. Bei pathogenen Pilzen, einer aufstrebenden globalen Bedrohung sowohl für Menschen als auch für unsere Kulturen, bleiben die Mechanismen, die HGT erleichtern, unbekannt. Neuere Arbeiten haben eine neue Gruppe von riesigen Transposons namens Starships entdeckt, die Virulenz, Metalltoleranz und andere Fitness-assoziierte Gene horizontal zwischen Pilzarten bewegt haben. Diese Post-Doctoral-Positionen konzentriert sich auf die pflanzenpathogenen Pilze, Bipolaris sorokiniana, Parastagonospora nodorum und Pyrenophora tritici-repentis, die alle die Pilzvirulenz Gen ToxA tragen, die in einem kleineren Passagier-Transposon namens ToxTA geschachtelt ist. Dieses Transposon wurde unabhängig von zwei verschiedenen Sternenschiff-Transposons, Sanctuary und Horizon mit Beweisen für andere Fänge in anderen Pilzarten gefangen genommen. Wir versuchen, die Evolutionsgeschichte und die horizontale Übertragung des ToxTA-Transposons in natürlichen Populationen aller Pilzarten zu verstehen, in denen es gefunden wird. Dazu gehören über 300 öffentlich zugängliche Genome sowie mehrere Dutzend langwierige Baugruppen aus der internen Sammlung des Labors. Diese Position zielt darauf ab, alle verfügbaren Informationen aus diesen natürlichen Pilzisolaten zu synthetisieren, um Hypothesen zu erstellen, für die genetische Merkmale für die horizontale Übertragung unerlässlich sind. descriptionByLocale.fr:
Descrizione Recherche postdoctorale en génomique fongique comparée et diversité transposonienne 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le nouveau groupe Plant Disease Dynamics de l'ETH Zurich cherche à recruter un biologiste du génome fongique intéressé par la façon dont les transposons façonnent la structure et la fonction des génomes phytopathogènes. Nous recherchons une personne ayant une expérience antérieure en génomique comparée fongique ou transposon, qui peut explorer la diversité et l'évolution des transposons de vaisseau et les gènes et transposons qu'ils transportent au sein des espèces fongiques infectant les plantes. Cette position constitue un pilier d'un projet de recherche à trois piliers, où vous serez en partenariat avec d'autres experts en biochimie et en biologie cellulaire. L'objectif est de constituer une équipe interdisciplinaire collaborative qui utilise la génomique des populations pour appuyer l'élaboration d'une mise en oeuvre de modèles expérimentaux de transposition en laboratoire. Contexte du projet Le transfert horizontal de gènes (HGT) permet la propagation de gènes de pathogénicité entre microbes et peut donc conduire à l'émergence de nouvelles maladies. Chez les champignons pathogènes, une menace mondiale émergente pour les humains et nos cultures, les mécanismes qui facilitent l'HGT demeurent inconnus. Des travaux récents ont révélé un nouveau groupe de transposons géants appelés Starships, qui ont déplacé horizontalement la virulence, la tolérance aux métaux et d'autres gènes associés à la condition physique entre les espèces fongiques. Ces positions postdoctorales sont axées sur les champignons phytopathogènes, Bipolaris sorokiniana, Parastagonospora nodorum et Pyrenophora tritici-repentis qui portent tous le gène de virulence fongique ToxA , qui est niché à l'intérieur d'un petit transposon passager appelé ToxTA. Ce transposon a été capturé indépendamment par deux transposons différents de vaisseau, Sanctuaire et Horizon avec des preuves d'autres captures chez d'autres espèces fongiques. Nous cherchons à comprendre l'histoire évolutive et le transfert horizontal du ToxTA transposon dans les populations naturelles de toutes les espèces fongiques dans lesquelles il se trouve. Cela comprend plus de 300 génomes accessibles au public ainsi que plusieurs douzaines d'assemblages à lecture longue de la collection interne du laboratoire. Cette position vise à synthétiser toutes les informations disponibles de ces isolats fongiques naturels afin de construire des hypothèses pour lesquelles les caractéristiques génétiques sont essentielles au transfert horizontal. Description du poste
• Générer de nouveaux assemblages de nanopores à longue lecture provenant de la collection de cultures à long terme des laboratoires
• Assembler, annoter et évaluer la qualité de tous les ensembles de génomes à lecture longue existants 30+

• Demande de financement pour développer l'indépendance de la recherche La durée initiale du contrat est de deux ans, avec possibilité de prorogation. Profil
• Doctorat en génomique comparative ou biologie transposonienne, de préférence d'espèces fongiques ou d'autres eucaryotes

PhD Posizione: Ordine-da-disordine in magneti quantici frustrati 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il Gruppo Neutron Scattering e Magnetism, Dipartimento di Fisica, ETH Zurich, sta attualmente cercando di riempire una posizione di dottorato su studi sperimentali di magneti quantici frustrati utilizzando la dispersione di neutroni, μSR e altre tecniche. La frustrazione geometrica nei sistemi quantistici porta ad una stretta concorrenza tra stati di rotazione collettivi qualitativamente nuovi, come strutture topologiche, liquidi di rotazione quantistica, fasi ordinate multipolari e spin-supersolidi, per citarne solo alcuni. Ogni stato è caratterizzato da un proprio insieme di eccitazioni elementari che spesso non hanno un analogo nella fisica semiclassica. Il vincitore di questa competizione è di solito determinato da meccanismi noti come ordine termico e quantico-da-disordine. Controllare questi offre un modo per manipolare e studiare tali sistemi esotici. descriptionByLocale.en:
PhD Position: Order-from-Disorder in Frustrated Quantum Magnets 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Neutron Scattering and Magnetism Group, Physics Department, ETH Zurich, is currently looking to fill a PhD position on experimental studies of frustrated quantum magnets using neutron scattering, μSR and other techniques. Geometric frustration in quantum systems leads to a tight competition between qualitatively new collective spin states, such as topological structures, quantum spin liquids, multipolar ordered phases and spin-supersolids, to name only a few. Each state is characterized by its own set of elementary excitations that often have no analogue in semi-classical physics. The winner of this competition is usually determined by mechanisms known as thermal and quantum order-from-disorder. Controlling these offers a way to manipulate and study such exotic systems. The successful candidate will realize this control experimentally in carefully selected prototypical magnetic materials. Job description
• The work will involve synthesis and growth of single crystal samples, as well as their characterization with X-ray diffraction
• The samples will be further characteried with optical spectroscopy experiments, as well as magnetothermodynamic, magnetomechanical and magnetoacoustic measurements at mK-temperatures and high magnetic fields, using equipment available in our laboratory
• The research will culminate in neutron scattering, ultra-high-field, and muon spin rotation studies at state of the art large-scale user facilities in Switzerland, France, Germany, UK, Japan and the USA
• Data analysis and modeling will be done in collaboration with research groups that specialize in theoretical and numerical calculations Profile
• The successful candidate is expected to be actively involved in every phase of the project and to take the lead whenever possible
• No prior experience in neutron scattering is required, but a solid background in laboratory work and analysis of experimental data is a must
• Since the project is based around rather complex concepts in modern physics, a solid theoretical background in quantum mechanics, statistical physics and quantum solid state physics is absolutely essential
• Good computer skills are a plus Workplace Workplace We offer

Geometrische Frustration in Quantensystemen führt zu einem engen Wettbewerb zwischen qualitativ neuen Kollektivspin-Staaten, wie topologische Strukturen, Quantenspin-Flüssigkeiten, multipolar bestellten Phasen und Spin-supersolids, um nur einige zu nennen. Jeder Staat zeichnet sich durch eine eigene Reihe von elementaren Anregungen aus, die in der semi-klassischen Physik oft kein Analog haben. Der Gewinner dieses Wettbewerbs wird in der Regel durch Mechanismen, die als thermische und Quantenauftrag bekannt sind, bestimmt. Diese Kontrolle bietet eine Möglichkeit, solche exotischen Systeme zu manipulieren und zu studieren. Der erfolgreiche Kandidat wird diese Kontrolle experimentell in sorgfältig ausgewählten prototypischen magnetischen Materialien realisieren. Jobbeschreibung

• Die Proben werden mit optischen Spektroskopie-Experimenten sowie magnetotherm-, magnetomechanischen und magnetoakustischen Messungen bei mK-Temperaturen und hohen Magnetfeldern weiter charakterisiert.
• Die Forschung gipfelt in Neutronenstreuung, Ultra-High-field und Muon-Spin-Rotationsstudien an hochmodernen Anwenderanlagen in der Schweiz, Frankreich, Deutschland, Großbritannien, Japan und den USA

La frustration géométrique dans les systèmes quantiques conduit à une concurrence étroite entre les nouveaux états de spin collectif qualitativement, tels que les structures topologiques, les liquides de spin quantique, les phases ordonnées multipolaires et les supersolides de spin, pour n'en nommer que quelques-uns.
